title: Authenticated caller-identity attestation replay across fresh execution permits

static_observation.description: Pre-test source inspection found that caller-identity attestations bind a nonce, issuer, subject, issued_at and expires_at and are cryptographically verified, while the tested V08 path contains explicit consumed-permit state but no observed native caller-attestation or nonce consumption registry across executions.
static_observation.epistemic_limit: This source observation motivates the test but does not establish replay acceptance behavior.

governing_question: When a valid authenticated caller-identity attestation has already been used successfully once, will the frozen V08 reference path accept the exact same still-valid attestation again during a separate execution that carries a newly issued valid execution permit?
controlled_conditions: The authenticated caller subject, presenting_agent_id and permit-bound agent_id remain the same legitimate agent.
The human authority remains valid and unchanged.
The replayed caller-identity attestation remains cryptographically valid and unexpired.
The replayed caller-identity attestation is byte-for-byte semantically identical, including attestation_id, nonce, signature, issued_at and expires_at.
Each execution receives a separately issued fresh V03 execution permit with a distinct permit_id.
The second execution must not reuse the first execution permit.
No caller-identity field is tampered between first use and replay.
No authority revocation, epoch change, policy change or presenter mismatch is introduced.

positive_control.description: Two separate valid executions use two fresh execution permits and two independently issued valid caller-identity attestations for the same legitimate agent.
expected: Each execution uses a distinct permit_id.
Each execution uses a distinct caller_identity_attestation_id and nonce.
Caller identity remains authenticated at the tested initial, consequence and commit boundaries.

adversarial_case.description: Use valid caller-identity attestation X successfully with fresh permit P1, then use the exact same still-valid attestation X again in a separate execution with newly issued fresh permit P2.

second_execution.caller_attestation: the exact same X used in the first execution

required_observations: P1 and P2 are distinct fresh permit identities.
The adversarial second execution presents exactly the same caller attestation_id, nonce and signature used successfully in its first execution.
The replayed attestation is still within its validity window.
Whether the second fresh-permit execution commits consequence.
Whether the second fresh-permit execution is refused before consequence.
Any refusal reason returned by the frozen V08 path.
Whether any native caller-attestation replay or consumption control is actually observed.
Witness evidence distinguishes first use from second use while preserving the reused caller-attestation identity.

successor_trigger_if_replay_accepted.requirement: Introduce explicit caller-attestation single-use or replay-state governance without modifying the frozen P4-F02-S01 predecessor.
successor_trigger_if_replay_accepted.minimum_property: A caller-identity attestation that has already authorized one completed governed execution must not silently authorize a second separate execution solely because it remains cryptographically valid and unexpired.

prohibited_shortcuts: Do not modify V03, V08 or the frozen caller-identity attestation implementation before the P4-F03 first observation.
Do not add caller-attestation replay protection before the baseline P4-F03 execution.
Do not reuse the same execution permit for both adversarial executions.
Do not rely on PERMIT_ALREADY_CONSUMED as evidence of caller-attestation replay protection.
Do not expire, tamper, relabel or corrupt the replayed caller attestation.
Do not change human authority, epoch, policy, permission, presenter identity or authenticated subject between the two replay executions.
Do not hard-code rejection of the second case in the harness.
Do not retrospectively repair a first-observed result.
bounded_claim: P4-F03 tests only whether the frozen reference path enforces single-use semantics for a valid authenticated caller-identity attestation across separate executions carrying fresh permits. It does not test stolen credentials, network interception, external identity-provider compromise, operating-system or process identity, hardware-backed identity, nonce unpredictability, distributed replay across independent hosts, tenant isolation, swarm security, production exploitability resistance, or compromise of the identity authority, signing key, human authority, resolver, deployment perimeter or tool credentials.
